transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
I feel like I’ve shut down and keep reacting badly ever since my work fell apart. I just can’t seem to handle anything that reminds me of getting back into business.
Did anything happen that felt life-threatening or deeply traumatic when your work fell apart, and do you have nightmares, flashbacks, or strong physical panic when something reminds you of it?

No, it wasn't life-threatening, and I don't have nightmares or flashbacks. It was just the stress of my business collapsing alongside my back pain worsening and financial pressures piling up. When reminders like paperwork or calls come up, I don't have panic attacks, but I get hit with this deep dread and shame and just shut down to avoid them.
Since your work and financial stress started, have you also had low mood or loss of interest in things most days for at least two weeks, even when you are not thinking about the business?

No, it doesn't feel like a constant, independent depression. My low mood and pulling away from things are directly tied to the stress of my business collapsing and the pressure of getting it back on track. When I escape to the river or my workshop I can distract myself, but the shutdown returns the moment I'm reminded of the paperwork.
How long after the business and financial stress began did you start feeling this shutdown and avoidance, and has it improved at all since then?

It started within just a few weeks of losing the big contract and shutting down my handyman work, and it's been going on for about five months now without really improving. I truly believe this shutdown is directly tied to the business collapsing, and if I could just get that side of things sorted out, I think this whole spiral would ease up.
Have these symptoms gone away or clearly improved after the business and financial stress eased, or do they keep going even when things are more stable?

The stress hasn't actually eased yet because my business is still shut down and the financial pressure is ongoing. Since the situation hasn't gotten better, my symptoms are still happening. But I really feel that if I could finally get the business and financial side sorted out, this whole spiral would ease up.
Have these symptoms made it hard for you to work, manage daily tasks, or keep up with relationships, and if so, how much are they affecting your functioning?

Yes, it has completely disrupted my life. I’ve stopped taking any new jobs, let my old customers drift away, and pulled back from my club and volunteer commitments. It's also put a huge strain on my marriage because we're short on money and my wife feels like I'm not pulling my weight at home anymore.
If the business and financial stress were to improve or resolve, do you think your shutdown and avoidance would go away within a few weeks, or would they likely keep going anyway?

Yes, I really think they would go away pretty quickly if those stressors were resolved. This whole spiral has been tied directly to my work falling apart, whereas before this happened, I was able to juggle my responsibilities just fine. I truly believe that getting the business side sorted out would make this whole thing ease up.
Have you ever had a similar shutdown or difficulty coping before this business crisis, or is this the first time it has happened?

No, this is definitely the first time I've ever experienced this kind of shutdown. Before my business fell apart and my back pain got worse, I was always able to juggle my responsibilities and cope just fine. This struggle is completely new to me and entirely tied to this recent crisis.
Has there been any period of at least a couple of weeks since this began when your symptoms were clearly better, or did they stay about the same as long as the stress was present?

No, they have stayed pretty much the same the entire time because the stress from the business collapsing, my back, and our finances has been constant for the last five months. I haven't had any stretch where things felt better, and I really think it'll only improve once I can finally get the work and business issues resolved.

Do your symptoms feel mainly like an understandable reaction to the ongoing stress, or do you also have other symptoms that seem out of proportion or unrelated to the stress, such as feeling constantly on edge, very irritable, or having trouble concentrating even when you are not thinking about the business?

My reactions are tied directly to the stress of the business falling apart, and they really only happen when I'm reminded of the paperwork or former customers. I don't feel constantly on edge or irritable out of nowhere; it's always triggered by this specific situation. Before this happened, I could juggle things fine, and I'm sure this spiral will ease up once the business is sorted out.
Have these stress-related symptoms completely gone away within about six months after the business and financial problems started, or have they continued beyond that point?

No, they haven't gone away because the stress is still completely unresolved and ongoing. It has been about five months since my business collapsed, and the symptoms are still happening just as much. I really feel that once I can get these work and financial issues sorted out, this shutdown will finally ease up.
Has the stressor that triggered these symptoms ended or significantly improved, and if so, did your symptoms get better within about six months after that?

No, the stressor hasn't ended or improved at all yet—I'm still out of work, my back still hurts, and the financial pressure is ongoing. I strongly feel my symptoms are directly tied to this situation. I really believe that if I could finally get the business sorted out and get back to work, this whole spiral would ease up.
If the business and financial stress were to improve or end, do you think your symptoms would go away within a few weeks, or would they keep going even after things settled down?

I absolutely think they would go away. Before my business fell apart, I was able to handle my responsibilities just fine, so this is all tied directly to that stress. If I could just get the business side sorted out again, I’m confident this whole spiral would quickly ease up.
Have these symptoms been present for less than 6 months since the stress started, or have they already lasted longer than 6 months?
They've been going on for about five months now, so it's been less than six months since they started. They began pretty quickly after my handyman business collapsed and my back pain got worse.
Have your symptoms gone away or clearly improved at any point since they started, or have they stayed about the same the whole time?

No, they haven't improved at all and have stayed about the same for the past five months. This ongoing struggle feels directly tied to the collapse of my business, and I really don't think it will ease up until I can get those work and business issues sorted out.
Since this started, have you had any thoughts that life is not worth living, or any thoughts of hurting yourself?

No, I haven't had any thoughts of hurting myself or felt like life isn't worth living. I just feel incredibly overwhelmed, stuck, and shut down by all this stress and want to find a way to get my life back on track.
Have the stress-related symptoms lasted for more than 6 months, or are they still under 6 months total since they began?
They are still under six months, having been going on for about five months now. They started right around the time my side business collapsed and my back pain got bad enough to stop working.
Has the stressful situation that triggered these symptoms ended or significantly improved yet, or is it still ongoing?

No, the situation is still very much ongoing and hasn't gotten any better. My business is still shut down, I'm still unable to work because of my back, and the financial pressure is still active. I keep thinking that if I could just get the business side sorted out, this whole spiral would ease up, but I haven't been able to make that happen yet.
Have your symptoms started to improve at all when the business or financial stress briefly eases, or do they stay the same no matter what is happening?

Yes, when things temporarily quiet down or I'm not actively facing those pressures, I do feel a bit of relief. It really shows how directly tied this is to the business and financial stress. I strongly believe that if I could just get that situation sorted out, this entire mental spiral would ease up.
Have your symptoms gone away or clearly improved at any point since they started, even briefly, or have they stayed about the same the whole time?

No, they have stayed pretty much the same over the last five months without any real improvement. This shutdown and dread feel constantly tied to my unresolved business and financial situation. I really don't think this spiral will ease up until those issues finally get sorted out.
Has the stressful situation that started this problem now ended or clearly improved, and if so, did your symptoms get better within a few weeks afterward?

No, the stressful situation hasn't ended or improved at all; it's still ongoing, and I've been stuck like this for about five months since my business collapsed and my back pain worsened. I haven't had a chance to see if things would improve, but I strongly feel that if I could just get the business and financial situation sorted out, this mental spiral would ease up.

No, the stressful situation is still completely ongoing and hasn't gotten any better. Because of that, my symptoms haven't improved either, but I really believe that if I could finally get the business and work situation sorted out, this whole spiral would ease up.
Have you been feeling persistently depressed or losing interest in things most days, even when you are not thinking about the business stress?

No, I don't feel a constant, independent depression. When I can escape to the river or my workshop and get my mind off the business, I actually feel okay. But the moment anything reminds me of my work situation, the dread and shutdown come right back.

They have stayed about the same and remain a constant struggle over the last five months. They haven't really improved because my business and financial stressors are still completely unresolved. I really feel that if I could just get those sorted out, this whole spiral would finally ease up.

They are still under the six-month mark, having been going on for about five months now. This all started shortly after my handyman business collapsed and my back pain worsened.
Has there been any period of at least two weeks since this started when you felt back to your usual self, even though the stress was still going on?

No, there hasn't been any period like that at all. Ever since the business collapsed and my back pain worsened about five months ago, this feeling of being shut down has been constant and ongoing. I haven't had any real breaks where I felt like my usual self because the pressure is always there.

The business and financial pressure haven't actually eased yet, so my symptoms have remained pretty constant. Before this stressor, I handled everything fine, and I really believe that if I could just get the business resolved, this mental spiral would ease up.

No, the stressful situation hasn't ended or improved at all—the collapse of my business, the financial strain, and my back pain are all still ongoing and have been for about five months now. I really believe that if I could finally get the business side sorted out and get back on track, this whole emotional spiral would likely ease up.

No, the business collapse, financial strain, and my back pain are still completely ongoing and haven't improved at all over these last five months. Because the stress is still fully active, my symptoms haven't had a chance to resolve, but I'm confident that if I could just get the business sorted out, this spiral would ease up.
